title: Sentinel POC: Infosec Triage and Evidence Register
content:
Executive summary:

This document is the working evidence register and triage notes created during the Sentinel POC (customer: Sentinel Health) security workshop (2025-09). Purpose: provide a concise mapping from the customer's security questionnaire to Redwood controls, list the evidence artifacts we can deliver, and surface outstanding gaps and owners for remediation. This is a working artifact intended for the security review team, solutions engineering, and the Sentinel InfoSec reviewers.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: Hosted API + Dedicated (reserved capacity) integration for a pilot environment. No on-prem/private deployment in scope for this POC.
- Data flow includes customer app -> Redwood hosted inference endpoint (TLS) -> optional dedicated GPU pool for model serving.
- Assumption: Sentinel will not store PII in prompts for the pilot; we have documented mitigation recommendations in the "Operational mitigations" section.

Questionnaire response highlights (summary):
- Encryption in transit: Provided narrative describing TLS 1.2+ termination at edge + mTLS for Dedicated peering. Evidence: certs and load-balancer TLS config.
- Encryption at rest: Redwood KMS-backed envelope encryption for S3 and DB backups. Evidence: KMS key policy extracts and S3 bucket policy sample.
- Access controls: RBAC via console and tokenized API keys; short-lived tokens for service accounts recommended. Evidence: access-review report (sample).
- Logging & auditability: Tracing hooks and per-call metadata captured; logs retained per POC retention (30 days). Evidence: sample trace JSON and centralized logging export config.
- Key management: Integration details for customer KMS/HSM discussed; evidence includes KMS integration design doc.
- Vulnerability management: Patch cadence and CVE triage process documented; evidence: monthly patch report excerpt.

Evidence register (key artifacts we can deliver):
- sentinel_network_arch_diagram_v1.pdf  -- annotated network diagram showing NAT, VPC peering for Dedicated, and control plane separation.
- dedicated_peering_config_example.yaml  -- sample Cloud config for dedicated peering and firewall rules.
- kms-integration-snippets.txt  -- key policy excerpts and IAM bindings for envelope encryption.
- access-review-2025-09.csv  -- redacted sample of user/service account access listing and last activity.
- audit-trace-log-sample.json  -- single-request trace showing route, model, cost, and token breakdown.
- s3-bucket-policy-sample.txt  -- least-privilege policy used during the POC evidence bucket.
- dependency-sbom-sentinel-poc.csv  -- SBOM summary for container images used in the Dedicated runtime.
- vulnerability-patch-log-2025-08.txt  -- CVE triage and remediation notes.
- least-privilege-iam-matrix.xlsx  -- Excel export showing role mappings and permissions.
- config-scan-report-sentinel-2025-09.pdf  -- results from automated config scanning (internal tool).

Mapping: questionnaire item -> Redwood artifact (high level):
- Q: How is data encrypted at rest? -> A: KMS-backed AES256 envelope encryption; evidence: kms-integration-snippets.txt, s3-bucket-policy-sample.txt
- Q: How are secrets protected in deployment? -> A: KMS + ephemeral tokens; evidence: dedicated_peering_config_example.yaml + token-rotation-overview.md (attached)
- Q: How do you isolate customer workloads? -> A: Dedicated GPU pools, network isolation, separate VPCs for dedicated; evidence: sentinel_network_arch_diagram_v1.pdf, dedicated_peering_config_example.yaml

Workshop notes (2025-09-10 session):
- Attendees: Priya R (Redwood SEC), Evan O (Solutions Eng), Maya C (Customer Sec), Luca M (Infra Eng), Jordan B (Sentinel Sec).
- Key customer asks:
  * Proof of in-flight encryption and mutual auth for Dedicated peering.
  * Demonstrable separation of telemetry between tenants (sample trace showing tenant_id scoping).
  * Confirmation that KV cache data is ephemeral and not written to durable storage.
- Actionable follow-ups agreed live:
  1) Provide KMS policy snippets customized for Sentinal's account (owner: Priya) - due 2025-09-16.
  2) Export a redacted access review and service-account list (owner: Evan) - due 2025-09-12.
  3) Produce a short demo (video + script) that shows a request routed to Dedicated pool and fallback to hosted variant on capacity — includes logs (owner: Luca) - due 2025-09-22.
  4) Validate retention and purge cadence for traces and logs for pilot (owner: Maya) - due 2025-09-14.

Open findings & risk register (triage level):
- F1 (Medium): No formal SLA for log retention beyond POC; mitigation: configure retention policy and include in MOU. Owner: Maya.
- F2 (Low): Some demo artifacts include identifying metadata — need redaction. Owner: Evan.
- F3 (High): Customer requested HSM-backed tenant keys for production; not in-scope for POC. Recommendation: propose Dedicated + KMS with Bring-Your-Own-Key in next-phase proposal. Owner: Priya.

Operational mitigations recommended for POC:
- Enforce prompt-hygiene: sample preprocessing to scrub known PII patterns before sending to Redwood endpoints.
- Enable per-route token scoping and short TTLs for service API keys used in the demo.
- Apply read-only IAM roles for Sentinel contacts who only need log access.

Deliverables attached to this register (links and s3 paths in linked_artifacts):
- Evidence tarball: s3://redwood-poc-evidence/sentinel/2025-09/evidence_bundle_v1.tar.gz
- Demo video + script: s3://redwood-poc-evidence/sentinel/2025-09/demo_fallback_v1.mp4
- Redacted access export: s3://redwood-poc-evidence/sentinel/2025-09/access_review_redacted.csv

Next steps & timeline:
- Target: close all POC-level findings and deliver final evidence bundle by 2025-09-25.
- Post-POC: prepare a production security design that covers BYOK HSM, extended retention SLAs, and formal SOC2/ISO artifacts if Sentinel chooses Dedicated >3 months.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: Priya Raman (priya@redwood.ai) — owning evidence delivery and security responses.
- Secondary: Evan Ortiz (evan@redwood.ai) — solutions eng / demo artifacts.

Notes (working):
- This register is intentionally concise — detailed attachments contain the canonical evidence. If a customer asks for a formal binder, we will assemble a PDF with signatures and include a one-page control mapping.
- Additions to the evidence set should be appended as new files in s3 and tracked via the INFSEC Jira ticket list (see linked_artifacts).
